## Keywords

{{< glossary app-package process loading refresh-rate resolution latency bandwidth cloud-gaming thermal-throttling >}}

## Think · Why is there a loading screen?

The game is already installed on the phone.
**Why must we wait before it starts?**

::: {.answer}
Code and assets must be copied from slow **storage** into fast **memory**.
:::

## 2.1 From the store to the first frame

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
- package: **AAB/APK** (Android) · **IPA** (iOS)
- install → storage · launch → **process** in RAM
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
![](images/launch.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Cheap phone, slow loading

1.5 GB of assets.

::: {.reveal}
1. 1500 MB/s → **1 s**
2. 150 MB/s → **10 s**
3. same game: 10× slower, only because of storage speed
:::

## Watch out · Storage size is not speed

- capacity → how many games fit
- **speed** → how fast they load
- **memory** → how much stays loaded

## Try it 1 · Install, launch, load

a) uploaded to Google Play?
b) iOS package?
c) installing fills…?
d) a program in execution?
e) 1.5 GB at 150 MB/s?
f) game restarts after a break?

::: {.answer}
a) AAB
b) IPA
c) storage
d) process
e) 10 s
f) the OS terminated its process
:::

## 2.2 The frame on real hardware

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
- CPU: logic, commands · GPU: pixels
- parallel → **the slower one sets the frame time**
- seen = min(frame rate, **refresh rate**) · **resolution** = GPU work · no fan → **throttling**
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
![](images/cpu-gpu-pipeline.png)
:::
::::

## Example · What limits the frame rate?

120 Hz display · CPU 12 ms · GPU 9 ms.

::: {.reveal}
1. frame time = slower = **12 ms**
2. 1000 / 12 ≈ **83 fps**
3. **CPU-bound**: lower resolution would not help
:::

## Try it 2 · Frames, displays, heat

a) 120 Hz, 70 fps: images per second?
b) CPU 12 ms, GPU 9 ms: fps?
c) the limiting processor?
d) pixels of 1080 × 2400?
e) slows down when hot?

::: {.answer}
a) 70
b) about 83 fps
c) the CPU
d) about 2.6 million
e) thermal throttling
:::

## 2.3 Where the game is computed

![](images/where-game-runs.png)

## Example · Adding up the input lag

::: {.reveal}
1. local: 10 + 17 + 17 ≈ **44 ms**
2. cloud: + round trip 40 + video 15 ≈ **99 ms**
3. ~100 ms: fighting game ✗ · card game ✓
:::

## Try it 3 · Near or far?

a) game on a server, phone shows video?
b) phones run it, server keeps the state?
c) action → result delay?
d) data per second?
e) 44 + 40 + 15?
f) suffers most from lag?

::: {.answer}
a) cloud gaming
b) client–server
c) latency
d) bandwidth
e) about 99 ms
f) a fighting game
:::

## 2.4 Device classes for gaming

![](images/devices.png)

## Comparing the classes

| | Input | Power | Sessions |
|---|---|---|---|
| phone / tablet | touch, sensors | battery, no fan | short |
| PC | keyboard, mouse | mains, fans | long |
| console | gamepad | mains, fans | long |
| cloud | any | server | needs a fast network |

## Try it 4 · Which device class?

a) gamepad, TV, fixed performance?
b) keyboard, mouse, widest range?
c) touch, battery, pocket?
d) any screen, fast network?

::: {.answer}
a) console
b) PC
c) smartphone
d) cloud gaming
:::

## Game challenge · The class survey

- most: Android phones · cheapest reads 120 MB/s
- some iPhones, laptops · one console
- two cloud players · one with a 90 ms round trip
- one game for all · work **alone**

## Try it 5 · One game, many devices (harder)

a) 600 MB level on the cheapest phone?
b) cloud lag with 90 ms round trip?
c) console input?
d) throttling matters most?
e) iPhone package?

::: {.answer}
a) 5 s
b) 149 ms
c) gamepad
d) smartphone
e) IPA
:::

## Summary

- install → storage · launch → process in RAM
- storage speed → loading time
- slower of CPU/GPU sets the frame rate
- phones throttle
- cloud: + latency, needs bandwidth
- adapt the game to each device class
